title: Interleaved-turn compaction scheduler with model-priority-aware KV pinning
creator: Maya Gupta
description: Tune the continuous-batching scheduler to better handle interleaved short and long prompt/response patterns by compressing slot usage, smoothing KV residency, and applying model-priority-aware KV pinning. Goal: reduce GPU memory churn and tail latency for mixed-length workloads without hurting throughput or quality.
background: We observe that customer workloads with interleaved short and long turns cause frequent KV cache thrashing and GPU slab fragmentation. Current continuous-batching heuristics prioritize latency for short requests but evict KV entries aggressively, causing long-turn requests to suffer high recompute and increased tail latency. Existing tickets focus on length-aware batching and prefetch; this ticket explores slot-level compaction combined with selective KV pinning to stabilize residency for high-priority model variants.
proposal: 1) Implement a slot compaction stage inside the continuous scheduler that can merge adjacent short-turn slots destined for the same GPU to free contiguous slab space. 2) Introduce a KV residency smoothing policy: KV entries get an inertia score (age + access frequency) and are protected from eviction for a tunable watermark window. 3) Add model-priority-aware pinning: for critical model variants (low-quantization or high-quality serving), pin a small fraction of KV pages even under pressure while applying opportunistic compression for best-effort variants. 4) Expose runtime flags and per-customer policies to tune watermarks and pin budgets.
acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end rollout that can be toggled per cluster and per model variant.
- 10-30% reduction in 95th/99th token-latency for mixed interleaved workloads in our lab replay (baseline: current continuous scheduler).
- No >5% throughput regression at P95 for synthetic throughput tests.
- Dashboards showing KV hit-rate lift and reduced GPU slab fragmentation metrics.
- Code review + integration tests + a canary rollout plan documented.
implementation_notes:
- Scheduler changes live in the continuous-batcher control loop: add a compaction pass after admission but before slot assignment.
- KV store changes: add "inertia_score" field (int) maintained on access; eviction checks consult inertia_score with watermark thresholds.
- GPU allocator: implement a fast path for contiguous slab reclamation after compaction using existing slab-manager APIs.
- Pinning: use per-GPU pin budget tracked in allocator telemetry; pins should be best-effort and revokeable under critical out-of-memory events.
- Keep changes behind runtime feature flags: scheduler.compaction.enabled, kv.smoothing.window, kv.pin.budget.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for compaction logic and inertia_score decay.
- Integration local replay with mixed-turn trace (customer A and internal mixlen traces).
- Stress test with tail-heavy synthetic workload (95/99 latency and slab fragmentation metrics).
- Canary on 3% of production traffic for one low-risk shard group with detailed telemetry.
- Load rollback exercise: force memory pressure to validate eviction/revocation paths.
metrics:
- KV hit rate (overall and per-model-variant).
- GPU slab fragmentation ratio (free contiguous bytes / total GPU slab).
- Token-level P50/P95/P99 latency.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) and successful request ratio.
- Number of pinned pages and pin-revoke events.
risks:
- Over-pinning could cause OOM on worst-case multi-tenant bursts. Mitigation: tight default pin budget and emergency revoke path.
- Compaction passes add CPU overhead; need microbenchmarks.
- Smoothing inertia may keep stale KV entries longer, increasing cache miss for shifting contexts. Mitigation: decay function and adaptive windowing.
- Quality regression if model-priority mapping incorrect; require per-customer validation and opt-out.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged internal canary on dev cluster.
2) Canary on low-load production shard (3%) for 48h, monitor defined metrics; rollback on any >10% latency regression or increased OOMs.
3) Expand to 10% for 72h if stable.
4) Gradual ramp by shard and region, with runtime knobs for pin budget per-customer.
5) Post-rollout: observe for 2 weeks and revert if >5% throughput regression at P95.
